newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lernout & Hauspie details new share issues.
newsitem.headline: Lernout & Hauspie details new share issues.

text.p: Belgian, Nasdaq-listed speech technology firm Lernout & Hauspie will issue a maximum of about 1.8 million new shares over the next few months as a result of operations announced on Wednesday and an acquisition due to be completed in June, the company told Reuters.

L&H said earlier on Wednesday that it was acquiring German translation machine maker GMS for around $14.7 million, paying $10.7 million in cash and $4 million in new common stock. It said it had also issued, via a private placement, $32 million of preferred stock, which could be converted into 1,250,000 shares of common stock.

A spokesman told Reuters the preferred stock could be converted according to a fixed timetable: 20 percent after 90 days, 20 percent after 120 days, 20 percent after 150 days, 20 percent after 180 days and 20 percent after 210 days.

Wednesday's news follows the announcement in April of plans to buy U.S. speech firm Kurzweil for $53 million, of which 80 percent in cash and 20 percent in common stock. The transaction is due to be completed in June.
The spokesman said that, on the basis of L&H's current share price, the common stock to issued as a result of the GMS and Kurzweil deals would amount to around 600,000 new shares.
He stressed that Lernout did not expect any of the new shares being issued to dilute 1997 earnings and the acquisitions would bring additional revenues to the company.
